_about: Packages the installers add to `pip install -e .[all,dev]` on each platform, because pyproject.toml cannot
carry them: forks installed from a git tag or a GitHub release (docs/PLATFORMS.md section 4) and platform
pins. scripts/install_windows.ps1, install_macos.sh and install_linux.sh read this file, and so does
`quantabench-cli update` (Help > Check for updates...): after a pull that changes an entry it reinstalls that
package, and --upgrade-packages keeps all of them. packages: requirement strings. only_binary: names passed as
--only-binary (never build from source). find_links: package name -> URL passed as --find-links; point it at
a new release and Update reinstalls that package, even when the version number stays the same.
Keep this file ASCII: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads it as ANSI.
programs: external programs the platform's installer downloads with --with-engines (-WithEngines): url, the
archive's sha256, the exe inside it and the release; the exe becomes this machine's engine path.

windows._why: FORK-1: dxtb ported to tad-libcint 0.4 (GFN2, polarizability, IR intensities). FORK-2: tblite wheels (PyPI has none for Windows).

gxtb._why: RANK-2: the rank step's g-xTB (rank_method gxtb, gxtb+cpcm, auto), the official grimme-lab/g-xtb v2.0.1 build of xtb, a preliminary release (docs/ENGINES.md). License GPL-3.0 (xtb itself LGPL-3.0): the installer downloads it for you and QuantaBench runs it as a separate program, never bundled. --with-engines (-WithEngines) downloads url, checks sha256 (the archive's; exe_sha256 is the executable's, as chem/eng_gxtb.py KNOWN_BUILDS lists it), unpacks it under the programs folder and sets exe as this machine's gxtb path. Its DLLs sit next to xtb.exe; QuantaBench puts that folder first on PATH when it runs it.

macos._why: FORK-1: PyPI's dxtb cannot use tad-libcint on macOS. tblite: never build from source (its newest wheels need macOS 15).

crest._why: FORK-5: conda-forge's osx-arm64 crest 3.0.2 links Apple's Accelerate and fails every optimization of 19+ atoms (docs/ENGINES.md). This is the fork's macOS build (brandonbtm29/crest, branch qb/macos, workflow qb-macos). install_macos.sh --with-engines downloads url, checks sha256, unpacks it under ~/Library/Application Support/QuantaBench/programs and sets exe as this machine's CREST path.
crest.built_by: brandonbtm29/crest Actions run 42295799792 (qb-macos, fork commit 12eb61d), artifact crest-macos-arm64, released unchanged as qb-v3.0.2-macos1 on 2026-11-07

gxtb._why: RANK-2: the rank step's g-xTB (rank_method gxtb, gxtb+cpcm, auto), the official grimme-lab/g-xtb v2.0.1 build of xtb, a preliminary release (docs/ENGINES.md). License GPL-3.0 (xtb itself LGPL-3.0): the installer downloads it for you and QuantaBench runs it as a separate program, never bundled. --with-engines (-WithEngines) downloads url, checks sha256 (the archive's; exe_sha256 is the executable's, as chem/eng_gxtb.py KNOWN_BUILDS lists it), unpacks it under the programs folder and sets exe as this machine's gxtb path. The arm64 archive has no libgcc_s.1.1.dylib, which its libgfortran needs (dyld stops at once on a Mac without Homebrew's gcc): install_macos.sh copies conda-forge's from the qb-tools environment into its lib folder (checked on the MacBook 2026-11-11: the same energies as the Linux build to 1e-12 Eh).

linux._why: GFN2-xTB in PyPI's dxtb needs tad-libcint below 0.4 (0.4 needs the dxtb fork; docs/INSTALL.md).

gxtb._why: RANK-2: the rank step's g-xTB (rank_method gxtb, gxtb+cpcm, auto), the official grimme-lab/g-xtb v2.0.1 build of xtb, a preliminary release (docs/ENGINES.md). License GPL-3.0 (xtb itself LGPL-3.0): the installer downloads it for you and QuantaBench runs it as a separate program, never bundled. --with-engines (-WithEngines) downloads url, checks sha256 (the archive's; exe_sha256 is the executable's, as chem/eng_gxtb.py KNOWN_BUILDS lists it), unpacks it under the programs folder and sets exe as this machine's gxtb path. The Linux build is statically linked.
